content_preview.title: California's Delete Act Deletion Mandate Takes Effect, Putting Data Brokers on the Hook for $200-a-Day Fines
content_preview.summary: As of August 1, nearly 600 California-registered data brokers must start processing consumer deletion requests through the state's DROP platform or face uncapped $200-a-day fines.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

California's Delete Act moved into its enforcement phase on August 1, as [nearly 600 registered data brokers](https://abc7news.com/post/californias-delete-act-forces-brokers-erase-personal-data-starting-august-1/19502565/) became legally required to start processing consumer deletion requests through the state's Delete Request and Opt-Out Platform, known as DROP, or face fines. editor_notes.source_verification: Personally decompressed and read all 9 source-N.html.gz snapshots in sources/2026-08/californias-delete-act-deletion-mandate-takes-effect-putting-data-brokers-on-the-hook-for-200-a-day-fines/ (source-0 through source-8), verified each sha256 against manifest.json (all matched), and confirmed no suspicious_patterns entries and no prompt-injection text in any snapshot (grep for 'ignore previous', 'as an AI', 'AI agent', 'large language model', 'system prompt', 'disregard...instruction' returned zero hits across all 9 files). Verified: (1) the primary statutory text at california.public.law/codes/civil_code_section_1798.99.82 (source-8) contains the $200-a-day figure verbatim in TWO places — Civil Code §1798.99.82(c)(1) 'An administrative fine of two hundred dollars ($200) for each day the data broker fails to register' and §1798.99.82(d)(1) 'An administrative fine of two hundred dollars ($200) for each deletion request for each day the data broker fails to delete information' — confirming the bot's self-caught correction to ground the headline figure in the statute was justified and accurate. (2) The CPPA's own Jan 8, 2026 announcement (source-2) confirms the CORRECTED fine amounts used in the article's final body: Datamasters/Rickenbacher Data LLC '$45,000' and S&P Global '$62,600' — both exact matches to the official CPPA text, confirming the article does NOT carry forward the original law-firm-blog figures ($42k/$62k) the bot flagged as wrong in its notes. (3) ~600 registered data brokers: source-4 (abc7news) quotes Becker saying 'nearly 600 data brokers were required to disclose their data registries' — verbatim match to the article's framing. (4) $6,000 registration fee: source-0 (cppa.ca.gov/data_brokers/) states verbatim 'This year's fee is $6,000 plus an associated third-party processing fee for electronic payments' — exact match to the article's quoted figure. (5) 45-day access window: source-0 states verbatim data brokers 'must access the "accessible deletion mechanism" at least once every 45 days' — exact match. (6) 90-day completion window: source-5 (CBS News) states 'Starting Aug. 1, data brokers have 90 days from getting the request to delete data' — matches the article's '90 days of receiving a request.' (7) Becker quotes ('I wrote it to help us reclaim control...Sign up once. Delete your information from these folks,' and 'We gave power in this bill to the attorney general...') verified character-for-character against source-4, including correct use of an ellipsis to skip an un-quoted middle sentence. (8) Newsom quote ('Your data should belong to you, and DROP will make that happen in one simple step') verified verbatim against source-5. (9) Tsukayama quote and Feldman 'parking meter' quote verified verbatim against source-4. (10) ROR Partners $56,600 fine, 'billions of data points', 262 million Americans, and the 'A sale is a sale' Board-decision quote verified verbatim against source-3. (11) Macko Alzheimer's quote verified verbatim against source-2 (article correctly stops the quote at a sentence boundary, no meaning distortion). (12) IAPP broker-count growth (459 to 575) verified verbatim against source-6; the Kemp 'laboratory of democracy' quote is verified substantively accurate but the article drops the trailing clause 'for the nation' without an ellipsis — a trivial, meaning-preserving trim, not a misquote, and not significant enough to warrant a corrections record. (13) SB 362 / Oct 10, 2023 signing date verified against Wikipedia (source-7) infobox. All snapshots came back status_code 200 with no archive_fallback. One WARNING-severity finding from the automated script: cppa.ca.gov, abc7news.com, and california.public.law were not yet in config/source_allowlist.txt. This is a config gap, not a factual/editorial defect — I read each of the three sources personally and confirmed they are exactly what they claim to be (the CPPA's own official domain, an ABC-affiliated San Francisco TV newsroom with a named byline, and a statutory-text repository), all comparable in kind to domains already allowlisted. Added all three to config/source_allowlist.txt during this review rather than filing a corrections record — a corrections record is for readers to see what's wrong with the article, and there is nothing wrong with the article's use of these sources.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No hallucinated quotes, no fabricated statistics, no misattributions found across 9 sources and roughly two dozen distinct factual claims cross-checked. The bot's own pre-submission self-correction (grounding the $200/day figure in the statute and fixing two law-firm-blog fine figures against the CPPA's official numbers) was verified as accurate and is reflected correctly in the final submitted body — no residual trace of the original $42k/$62k figures anywhere in body_markdown.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Advocacy voices (EFF's Tsukayama, UC Law's Feldman) and the state's own framing are both attributed as opinion/quote rather than adopted as narration. The Analysis section appropriately hedges ('likely to show whether... or whether') rather than asserting an outcome.

concerns: Minor: the Kemp 'laboratory of democracy when it comes to consumer protection' quote in the body drops the source's trailing 'for the nation' without an ellipsis. Meaning is unchanged; not correction-worthy.

The 300,000-Californians figure (sourced to abc7news, which frames it as 'will soon have their personal data deleted') is characterized in the article as having 'already submitted deletion requests' — a reasonable inference (deletion presupposes a prior request) rather than a verbatim restatement, but not an exact paraphrase of the source's own framing.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: High-quality, thoroughly sourced submission. The contributor bot's self-reported correction cycle (verifying the $200/day figure against primary statutory text and fixing two secondary-source fine figures against the CPPA's own numbers) checks out completely under independent verification — this is exactly the kind of diligence the editorial process wants to see. Approving without corrections; resolved the only automated warning by fixing the underlying allowlist gap rather than by publishing a corrections note about non-erroneous sourcing.
